conviction_note: Additive sum of four findings (-2.0 +2.5 -2.0 -0.5 = -2.0): the AI-consumption story that drove a +28% 20-day re-rating is measurably lower-quality than the headline (25% of the June CRR figure was giveaway credits, quietly restated in a furnished 8-K; gross margin 90%->88%) and GitLab has just shipped hard credit caps that suspend Duo, but that is partly offset by a guide that explicitly assumes no material Duo revenue against a company-confirmed accelerating consumption line, and by the fact that a +6.53 skew means the market already pays for downside here.

findings.finding: In a Reg FD 8-K furnished 2026-07-08, GitLab restated the Duo Agent Platform paid Consumption Run Rate it had touted five weeks earlier as 'nearly $20 million' down to approximately $15 million, because the calculation 'now excludes certain one-time credit incentives granted to paying customers' - i.e. roughly a quarter of the headline AI number the street heard in June was credits given away to existing paying seats, not incremental purchase.
findings.why_not_priced: The restatement was buried in a furnished (not filed) Item 7.01 8-K whose only exhibit is a 48-slide deck rendered as 48 JPEG images (exhibit991-businessupdat001.jpg through 048.jpg), so it is not machine-readable and not searchable; every write-up of that filing led on the forward number instead, e.g. Quiver headlined it 'GitLab Jumps as Investor Update Highlights Faster Consumption Growth and AI Product Traction'. If the market had priced the giveaway component, the sell-side previews into this print would be arguing about credit gross margin rather than 'Duo traction', and the stock would not be trading at $45.64 against a 28-broker consensus target of $38.92 with three brokers only just chasing it up from $35-36 in the last week of August.
findings.independence: Independent corroboration of the giveaway mechanic and its cost, from a different document: the Q1 FY27 call, where CEO William Staples described 'promotional credits that we've given in this first quarter of availability' letting developers 'experiment with Duo Agent platform before the organization needs to commit', and the Q1 release shows non-GAAP gross margin of 88% versus 90% a year earlier while CFO Jessica Ross attributed the 88% to favourable SaaS mix rather than inference cost - https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/06/03/gitlab-gtlb-q1-2027-earnings-transcript/ and https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260602438182/en/GitLab-Reports-First-Quarter-Fiscal-Year-2027-Financial-Results . NOTE: shares the 2026-07-08 8-K as a source with finding 2 below, which reads the same document in the opposite direction.

findings.finding: GitLab's FY27 guidance explicitly embeds no material Duo Agent Platform revenue contribution, yet the company went out of its way one month into Q2 to confirm paid CRR had gone from ~$15M at 30 April to above $20M at 30 June on the same restated basis - a ~33% step-up in two months on a line that is upside-only versus the guide.
findings.why_not_priced: A voluntary mid-quarter Reg FD business update is a management-confidence tell that aggregators record as a press-release row and nothing more; GTLB did not sustain a re-rating in July, and the +28.26% 20-day run-up in the baseline dates from the 26-27 August sector-wide AI-software melt-up, not from GitLab-specific consumption news. The clearest evidence it is unpriced is that the consensus Q2 revenue estimate (~$273.1-273.3M) sits inside the company's own $272-274M guide, i.e. the street is modelling a zero beat on a company whose Q1 revenue came in about four points above its guided growth rate - if the consumption upside were priced, estimates would sit above the guide, not on it.
findings.independence: The mid-quarter CRR trajectory itself comes from the 2026-07-08 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1653482/000165348226000145/gtlb-20260708.htm), which is the SAME document finding 1 rests on - flagging that explicitly; the independent leg here is the Q1 transcript, a different document, in which the CFO lists 'no material DAP revenue contribution in FY27' as one of four prudence items baked into the raised full-year guide.

findings.finding: GitLab 19.3, released 2026-08-20, made hard GitLab Credits usage caps generally available - subscription-level and per-user spend ceilings after which 'features that consume GitLab Credits, like GitLab Duo Agent Platform, are suspended until the next billing period' - and the same release cycle added a GitLab Dedicated AI Gateway letting enterprises connect their own inference models; both are direct concessions to customers who in GitLab's own public forum call the credit economics 'fundamentally broken' (one reported ~$10 of credits consumed by a single agentic task).
findings.why_not_priced: Release notes and a vendor support forum are not in any earnings feed, and neither is covered by the DevOps trade press write-ups of 19.3, which led on Secrets Manager and the AI gateway. This matters because the entire bull case for the H2 guide is an uncapped consumption ramp; a customer-settable ceiling that switches Duo off, plus a bring-your-own-model path for the highest-ARR (Dedicated) cohort, structurally caps monetisation per seat. If it were priced, the run-up would not have come with sell-side targets being marked up to $45-52 on 'early Duo Agent Platform traction' in the same week, and the previews would be debating cap attach rates.
findings.independence: Customer-side corroboration from a different source: the GitLab Duo forum thread 'Expensive AI', where paying users document credit burn ($5 for two code reviews on a $12 promotional balance; $57 for 5 credits with 18% consumed by one task) and ask for bring-your-own-API-key - https://forum.gitlab.com/t/expensive-ai/132493 , latest post 2026-05-14. NOTE: shares the 19.3 release notes with finding 4.

findings.finding: The scope of the credits wallet - and therefore of the CRR metric the market is treating as an AI-adoption gauge - is being broadened beyond AI: GitLab Secrets Manager is now 'an add-on billed through GitLab Credits' (19.3, 2026-08-20) and GitLab's own docs repository carries a commit dated 2026-08-26 titled 'Broaden GitLab Credits scope beyond Duo Agent Platform', on top of the CRR definition already having been changed once in July to add Flex and drop one-time incentives.
findings.why_not_priced: Nobody diffs a vendor's documentation git log. The consequence is that whatever consumption figure is given on this call and the next is not comparable to the 'nearly $20M' anchor the street wrote down in June, and any sequential jump will be part reclassification of non-AI add-on and compute billing. If the market had priced metric instability, an unaudited, twice-redefined internal run-rate would carry a discount in the coverage rather than being quoted as the AI proof point; instead it is the headline of every July-update write-up.
findings.independence: Independently visible in GitLab's published 19.3 release notes ('GitLab Secrets Manager is an add-on billed through GitLab Credits') - https://docs.gitlab.com/releases/19/gitlab-19-3-released/ - but that is the SAME document as finding 3's primary source, so treat findings 3 and 4 as one source cluster with two distinct mechanisms.

searched_and_found_nothing: Strategic-process / activist traffic: EDGAR shows only one passive SCHEDULE 13G/A (2026-07-28) since the last print, no 13D, and no 8-K of any kind between 2026-07-08 and today - so no pre-announcement, no second mid-quarter update, and nothing to support the January 2026 'buyout candidate' speculation

Insider Form 4 cluster: the only Q2/Q3 transactions are a routine 10b5-1 sale by CAO Simon Mundy (8,725 shares at $38 on 2026-08-07, plan dated 2025-06-23) and an automatic Class B-to-A conversion by director Godfrey Sullivan on 2026-08-21 - no discretionary selling into the +28% run-up
JiHu China JV: R&D attributed to the consolidated VIE was only $0.6M in Q1 FY27 vs $0.4M a year earlier, and there is no Q2 filing or 8-K indicating deconsolidation - too small to move the print

A second restructuring or further country-exit announcement after the 2026-06-02 Item 2.05 8-K (14% / ~350 people, 22 countries, $30-35M charge with ~$19M in Q2) - nothing new found, and management stated it 'had no sales presence in the geographies' exited, which removes the revenue-disruption angle I was chasing

Scale of the customer cost revolt: the GitLab forum 'Expensive AI' thread has only 9 replies and nothing after 2026-05-14, and I found no Reddit or HN thread of comparable specificity - so this is a documented irritation, not an escalating churn event, which is why finding 3 is sized at 2 points and not more

Pricing-page diff over time: about.gitlab.com returns HTTP 403 to this fetcher and web.archive.org is blocked, so I could not verify the $12 Premium / $24 Ultimate included-credit amounts or the promotion's end-date language from a primary page - those figures appear only in search snippets of about.gitlab.com/pricing/terms and are therefore NOT load-bearing in any finding above
Hiring-page / headcount diff after the June RIF - GitLab careers pages not reachable from this environment

Supplier or customer read-throughs given after 2026-06-02 that name GitLab specifically - nothing found beyond the generic 26-27 August software-sector AI relief rally that StockStory attributes the 8.5% single-day move to
baseline_tension: Net, my findings agree with the +6.53 skew and therefore are partly priced already, which is exactly why the number is -2.0 and not -6.0; the one thing that cuts against the baseline is that the guide explicitly assumes zero Duo revenue while consensus sits inside the company's own revenue guide, so the +28% run-up has re-rated the narrative without the estimates having moved.
